memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his inheritance. So Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite ever since, because he followed the Lord, the God of Israel, wholeheartedly. (Hebron used to be called Kiriath Arba after Arba, who was the greatest man among the Anakites.) Then the land had rest from war - Josh 14:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua blesses Caleb and grants him Hebron, and the writer explains why once more: "because he followed the Lord... wholeheartedly." That phrase, repeated yet again, is clearly the point God wants us to carry away. Caleb's wholehearted devotion, sustained across forty-five years, is honoured with the very inheritance he had trusted God for.

There is a lovely detail in the name. Hebron used to be called Kiriath Arba, after Arba, "the greatest man among the Anakites" — the greatest of the giants. The place named after the mightiest giant becomes the inheritance of the man who trusted God to defeat giants. Where the enemy's name once loomed largest, God planted the reward of faith.

And then, quietly, the chapter closes: "Then the land had rest from war." After all the battles, after Caleb's mountain is claimed, there is rest. This points us gently forward. Every faithful believer's journey through struggle and giants moves toward a promised rest — a rest that Joshua's generation tasted only in part, but that is fully ours in Christ (Heb 4:9-10). Caleb's story assures us that wholehearted trust in God is never wasted. The mountain is given, the giant's stronghold becomes home, and rest comes at last.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where might God want to give you "rest" on the very ground where you once faced giants?
- Does Caleb's honoured faith encourage you to keep trusting God wholeheartedly?
- How does the promise of rest in Christ steady you in your present battles?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that wholehearted trust in You is never wasted. Give me courage to face my giants, and bring me at last to the rest that is mine in Christ. Amen.
